sentences.text: This fish featured a highly elongated snout and sharp, bony plates on its mouth that formed a turtle-like beak.
The genus Rolfosteus was described by Dennis and Miles in 1979.
Researchers suggest the elongated snout may have enhanced its sense of smell and improved streamlining for hunting as a pelagic predator.
The turtle-like beak was used for cutting prey.
Fast jaw movement and specific jaw morphology allowed it to capture and swallow prey whole.
Rolfosteus is classified within the family Camuropiscidae, superfamily Incisoscutoidea, and the clade Coccosteomorphi.
Rolfosteus lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago in the Gogo Formation of Western Australia.
